valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 15 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a Sri Lankan group; weighted by 2025/26 profit attributable of the profitable segments (Annual Report 2025/26, segment note p. 166): Consumer Brands Rs 5.39bn (home and personal care, stationery) and Healthcare Rs 4.91bn (pharma distribution and manufacturing, hospitals), 52% / 48%. Mobility (Rs 0.86bn, 8%) left out because no sector beta for it could be read; the loss-making Others segment (leisure, head office) is not weighted. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-ins from web-search extracts of his global sector table (date not shown in the extract, so not confirmed as January 2026): Household Products unlevered, cash-corrected 0.77; Drugs (Pharmaceutical) 1.00 (used for all of Healthcare; no Hospitals row could be read). Weighted: 0.52 × 0.77 + 0.48 × 1.00 = 0.88. (3) Relevered with net debt Rs 11.9bn (30 Sep 2026) ÷ market value Rs 99.2bn (Rs 33.10 × 2,996mn shares) = 0.12 and 32.3% tax: 0.88 × (1 + 0.677 × 0.12) = 0.95. (4) Local 5-year betas: none found. StockAnalysis shows Beta (5Y) n/a; Simply Wall St 0.26 (April 2025) and Investing.com 0.36 give no period; TradingView 1.09 is a 1-year beta (ignored). Fewer than 3 usable sources, so step 4 can't be completed. (5) Higher of 0.95 and (no local figure) = 0.95. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file (including Hospitals and Transportation rows) and three verified local 5-year betas.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (15 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.95 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.0%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 16.5 / 15.5 / 14.5%.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (15 Nov 2026): cost of debt 9.77% (interest paid 0.753 ÷ average borrowings and leases 7.70, FY 2026), tax 32.3%, debt weight 10.7% (net debt Rs 11.9bn at Sep 2026, market cap Rs 99.2bn at Rs 33.10).

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 4% / 7% / 10%; supported 2.3% (reinvestment rate 10.7% × return on capital 21.2%, FY 2026). Base 4.7 and bull 7.7 pts above: kept because FY 2026 reinvestment was unusually low (cash built up for acquisitions) and FY 2027 reinvestment is already under way — Twiga bought for Rs 5.46bn, Rs 12.3bn into working capital and capex Rs 2.45bn against depreciation Rs 1.35bn in H1, Rs 2.0bn of capex contracted; profit kept × ROE gives 11.7%; and the DCF charges growth ÷ return on capital in reinvestment every year.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY 2026 figures recorded in this redo.

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.value: Bear 4% then 4% / Base 7% then 5% / Bull 10% then 6%
valuationInputs.reason: Five years, then long-run. Was 5 / 6 / 7% long-term only. Long-run below the 12.24% bond and WACC, reinvesting growth ÷ return on capital (29% / 28% / 29%).

valuationInputs.name: Return on new capital
valuationInputs.reason: FY 2026 return on capital 21.2% (after-tax operating profit ÷ opening equity and net debt); acquisitions such as Twiga dilute it.

valuationInputs.reason: Calculator FY 2026: operating cash 11.81 + after-tax interest 0.51 − maintenance 3.92 / 2.36 / 2.30 = 8.40 / 9.95 / 10.01, times 95% for minority shareholders, bear and base trimmed for this year's margin squeeze.

valuationInputs.name: After-tax operating profit (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 8.1bn / Base Rs 9.0bn / Bull Rs 9.7bn
valuationInputs.reason: Trailing operating profit Rs 13.99bn × (1 − 32.3%) = 9.47, owners' share about 9.0; bear 10% lower; bull assumes margins recover.

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. Bear = average capex booked FY 2025–26 (includes the Rs 1.9bn Thalawathugoda land, so high); base = depreciation and amortisation; bull = less impairment.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Ten-year average about 13%, five-year about 15.5%, last two years 17–18%; ROE path from 15 / 16 / 17%.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027 × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS Rs 0.98; H2 Rs 1.55 / 1.85 / 2.10 (last year 1.89). P/E = two-stage forward P/E justified at the cost of equity (payout 1 − growth ÷ ROE). Base 5% below the Rs 2.98 run-rate.

valuationInputs.name: Payout
valuationInputs.reason: 2025/26 payout 31.8%; after year five, 1 − growth ÷ ROE.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Justified P/B, residual income, P/E, whole-company DCF
valuationInputs.reason: Dividend model left out (payout a third); dividends shown as a reading.

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/redo HHL full). Research record rebuilt from the downloaded reports: FY 2026 and FY 2025 reinvestment figures added (depreciation and amortisation 2.36 / 2.00; capex booked 2.66 / 5.18, with the Rs 1.9bn Thalawathugoda land named as growth in FY 2025; working capital +0.54 / −3.78; acquisitions 0.19 / 0.69; operating profit 14.15 / 13.71; tax 32.3% / 34.5%; equity; borrowings, leases and cash; interest paid 0.75 / 1.27, operating section; dividends paid), R&D Rs 0.35bn (0.3% of revenue, no adjustment), H1 FY2027 capex, depreciation and interest. Earlier figures, reportsRead and change log kept. Beta 0.95 (provisional: Damodaran's site was blocked, so global sector betas from web-search extracts; no local 5-year beta found) gives cost of equity 18.0% (was 15.5% by hand) and WACC 16.8%. Capex-based supported growth 2.3%; growth 4 / 7 / 10% kept above it with reasons. DCF now whole-company at WACC less net debt: weighted 29.0 → 14.8; P/E 27.3 → 15.3 (justified 4.6 / 5.4 / 6.7x); P/B 20.0 → 17.4; residual income 20.5 → 16.5. Price ranges: the September report's six-month range conflicts with the June report; the June report's was used. Business tests 4 of 4, unchanged; category unchanged (watch list). Fair value Rs 24.20 → 16.00, buy Rs 20.60 → 13.60, strong buy Rs 18.20 → 12.00.
